items.title: Pseudo-Labels as Rewards, Not Targets: Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Semi-Supervised ASR
items.summary: Adapting ASR to a domain with only untranscribed audio typically relies on pseudo-labeling, a strong teacher transcribes the audio and a student is fine-tuned on it. We show that using the same pseudo-labels as a reward reference for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is more robust to label noise.

items.title: Supervised Source Separation of Electric Vehicle Interior Noise Using a Hybrid Transformer Architecture
items.summary: Decomposing a recorded vehicle interior signal into these source contributions is a prerequisite for targeted acoustic engineering, but requires effortful measurement campaigns as well as expertise in the field of transfer path analysis.

items.title: DIAL-S2ST: Learning Latency Control for Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation
items.summary: We propose DIAL-S2ST, a post-training method for learning inference-time latency control in simultaneous speech-to-speech translation models. Our approach reuses pretrained translation capabilities through self-distillation from lookahead predictions, while limiting the influence of large text distillation losses to account for the imitation gap.

items.title: X-Dubbing: Speech-to-Speech Translation under Temporal and Visual Constraints
items.summary: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video. In this paper, we propose X-Dubbing, which formulates the task as a joint problem of time-aware speech-to-text translation and video-aware text-to-speech.

items.title: When Do Self-Supervised Representations Help Speech Restoration?
items.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) representations are widely used in speech restoration (SR), and the prevailing trend is SSL feature cleansing: fine-tuning the SSL to recover clean features from degraded speech, then conditioning the restoration model on them.

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: Higher-order Ambisonics (HOA) is an attractive format for immersive spatial audio, but its high channel count and directional properties present significant audio coding challenges. We introduce SEMAC, which instead represents an Ambisonics signal by a quantized full-order directional energy envelope together with fewer CELT-coded transport channels.

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: Auditory attention decoding (AAD) seeks to identify the attended talker from brief noninvasive brain recordings by comparing neural responses with competing speech streams.

items.title: Melody Guidance for Audio Diffusion Models Without Retraining
items.summary: Controlling melody in audio generation normally requires training a conditional generative model on audio paired with pitch curves or MIDI notes. We instead guide an existing unconditional diffusion model, originally trained without melody inputs, to follow a target melody without retraining or modifying it.

items.title: ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Challenge
items.summary: This paper presents the ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Grand Challenge, the first community challenge dedicated to benchmarking speech enhancement from millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar vibrometry.

items.title: SURE-Tagger: Structured Speech Representations for Compositional Evaluation and Targeted Data Selection
items.summary: We introduce SURE-Tagger, a framework that constructs semi-structured speech representations with explicit attribute values, supplementary descriptions, and abstention under insufficient evidence. On Tag-Bench, SURE-Tagger achieves the highest scores on 25 of 29 evaluated dimensions for real speech and 24 of 29 for synthetic speech, outperforming caption-based baselines across structural and descriptive attributes.

items.title: Uni-Stream: A Unified Streaming Speech Language Model for Speech Synthesis and Recognition
items.summary: Unified streaming speech language models aim to support speech recognition and synthesis within a single model, enabling real-time human-computer interaction. We propose Uni-Stream, a unified streaming speech language model built on compact pretrained speech models.

items.title: MG-REPA: Multi-Granularity Representation Alignment for Generative Target Speaker Extraction
items.summary: Generative target speaker extraction (TSE) models achieve high-quality extraction, but suffer from considerably slow training convergence. For TSE, frame-level alignment leaves the global, time-invariant characteristics of the target speech implicit, whereas utterance-level alignment leaves the time-varying content implicit, even though extracting the target requires both.

items.title: NECTAR: Automatic Negative Clue Estimation via Centroid-Space Mapping for Target Speaker Extraction
items.summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. To derive this representation from the observed mixture, we analyze the relationship between the speaker representations of a speech mixture and its constituent speakers.

items.title: Concentrated Causal Influence, Distributed Diagnostic Information: Cognitive Impairment Decisions in Large Audio-Language Models
items.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) can assess cognitive impairment (CI) from speech, yet their answers reveal neither which internal components control the decision nor how much CI information is accessible in their representations.

items.title: DRAMA-Eval: A Benchmark for Context-Aware, Multi-Turn, Multi-Speaker Speech Generation
items.summary: Recent advances in speech generation are shifting toward context-aware, multi-turn, and multi-speaker synthesis. Beyond traditional zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS), modern systems in this domain primarily fall into three categories: instruction-controllable generation models, multi-turn dialogue models, and the audio branches of audio-visual generation models.

items.title: Input Bias Correction in Gaussian Process Regression
items.summary: In traditional Gaussian process (GP) regression, the inputs are typically assumed to be known, and uncertainty enters only through the measurements. When scalar fields are mapped using GP regression with measurements obtained from a mobile sensor, the inputs correspond to the estimated pose of the mobile sensor.

items.title: Distributed Swarm Morphogenesis with Neural Cellular Automata
items.summary: Swarm morphogenesis requires robots to assemble desired shapes through local interactions. We present a modular framework integrating neural cellular automata (NCA) with existing site selection and collision-aware control. Robots already in the formation update and share local NCA states to identify new attachment sites, enabling progressive growth without a predefined list of sites during deployment.

items.title: Silence Is Not Assurance: When Production Lane Keeping Assist Does Not Warn, and What It Costs
items.summary: Production lane keeping assist (LKA) systems tell the driver whether they detect the lane markings, but whether this displayed status reflects what the system perceives, and what happens when it does not, has not been examined in real-world driving.

items.title: Move, don't think: sample-efficient collision avoidance with lossy proximity sensors
items.summary: Data-driven robots must learn to avoid collisions with as few demonstrations as possible to avoid collecting large datasets of destructive collision examples. We explore whole-body proximity sensors as inductive biases for learning reflexive collision-dodging behavior and find that lossy sensors with low resolution were stronger biases than high-resolution coverage.

items.title: Emergent Cooperative Thermoregulation in Lunar Swarm Robotics
items.summary: Swarms of small robots are an attractive way to survey lunar caves and lava tubes. The 354 h lunar night drops the surface towards 95 K, and the radioisotope heaters that let single rovers survive it cannot be supplied at swarm scale. The swarm aggregates, and robots circulate between the sheltered core and the exposed rim, the same pair of behaviors with which emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter.

items.title: Full-Weight VLA Fine-Tuning Without an fp32 Master Copy Silently Erases Most Updates
items.summary: When a vision-language-action (VLA) model is fine-tuned with its trainable weights in bfloat16 (bf16) and no fp32 master copy, AdamW writes each update straight into bf16, silently rounding away any update smaller than 1/512 of a weight. In our LIBERO runs without the copy, a probe every 100 steps finds at least 79% of updates to bf16 weights erased.

items.title: Multimodal MPC via Bayesian Set Optimization for Dynamic Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects
items.summary: Dynamic manipulation of deformable linear objects (DLOs) remains challenging due to underactuated, high-dimensional dynamics, delayed deformation responses, and the presence of multiple feasible motions under obstacle constraints. This paper presents BM2PC, a Bayesian Multimodal MPC framework for agile manipulation of DLOs.

items.title: EgoForesight: Effectively Scaling Policy Learning with Noisy Egocentric Actions
items.summary: Scaling policy learning requires broad experience and reliable supervision. Egocentric videos broaden task and environment coverage, yet motion reconstruction and retargeting introduce noisy action labels.

items.title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion.

items.title: WorldMirror: Agentic Real-to-Sim Generation of Interactive Worlds from In-the-Wild Robot Demonstrations
items.summary: Meanwhile, in-the-wild robot demonstrations naturally provide diverse and realistic observations of real-world interactions. We introduce WorldMirror, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations.

items.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Real-world reinforcement learning has enabled contact-rich manipulation tasks to be trained directly on physical robots, but unsafe interactions during online learning remain a key barrier to practical deployment. We propose Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning (SEVI), a framework for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world policy learning.

items.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer
items.summary: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for learning robot behaviors aligned with human intent. In this work, we present PrefO2O, an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework that enables zero-shot PbRL on unseen target tasks without requiring any human feedback.

items.title: KiRoSe: Using Kinematic Data for Efficient Segmentation of Robot Demonstrations
items.summary: Segmenting robot demonstration data into disjoint temporal and semantic subsegments is valuable for learning, cleaning, retrieval, and analysis. In this paper, we introduce KiRoSe (Kinematics for Robot Segmentation), a novel framework that focuses on the companion stream of robot kinematic data.

items.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
items.summary: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

items.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
items.summary: What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models.

items.title: CuraLoc: Repository-Level Fault Localization via Planned Code Inspection
items.summary: Existing repository-level localization methods often let language models iteratively decide what code to inspect next, requiring repeated model calls and substantial token usage. Additionally, CuraLoc supports different model backbones, with strong localization accuracy demonstrated using both GPT-5.2 and GPT-6 Astra.

items.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
items.summary: We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. PaperScorer is strongest on the lowest and highest rated papers, while papers rated in the middle stay unpredictable for our models and frontier systems alike.

items.title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning
items.summary: We introduce PDF, a path-dependent client-selection framework based on the insight that retained clients are not equally valuable for unlearning. Upon an unlearning request, these histories identify and rank retained clients that are globally informative yet weakly coupled to the target, enabling retraining-based unlearning with only the top-$k$ clients over a small number of rounds.

items.title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
items.summary: To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction. Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks.

items.title: Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Model Inference via Per-Query Modality Selection
items.summary: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video, enabling stronger multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities, but often at substantial inference cost. Motivated by this, we study query-wise modality selection, which keeps the underlying Omni-LLM fixed while adaptively selecting which modalities to provide for each query.

items.title: Learning to Be Monitored: Causal Bounds and Intervention-Aware Post-Training Recipes for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring aims to detect potentially harmful behaviors in large language models (LLMs) from their CoTs. However, a target behavior observed under intervention is not necessarily caused by it, and we show that this metric can overestimate how often a monitor detects target behaviors actually caused by the intervention.

items.title: ConsMSA: Semantic Distribution Consistency Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
items.summary: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict human sentiments by integrating signals from different modalities such as text, video, and audio. To this end, we introduce ConsMSA, which explicitly formalizes semantic distribution consistency across both $\textit{intra}$- and $\textit{inter}$-modality, providing a consistency-aware mechanism for robust and efficient multimodal sentiment prediction.

items.title: When and How Does Muon Precondition? The Role of Structured Gradient Noise
items.summary: Muon has become a popular optimizer for large language model training, yet its theoretical foundations remain poorly understood. We first show, theoretically and empirically, that under the classical isotropic noise assumption, Muon offers no acceleration beyond a rescaling of the learning rate.

items.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
items.summary: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people.

items.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems
items.summary: However, ensuring the reliability and availability of microservice systems critically relies on effective anomaly detection, as failures and performance anomalies can quickly propagate across services and severely impact end-to-end system behavior.

items.title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization
items.summary: In offline model-based optimization (MBO), methods must improve designs using only a fixed dataset and no test-time access to the true objective. In this paper, we propose Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning (D2C) for offline MBO, which leverages the fact that deterministic sampling makes the reverse denoising chain differentiable with respect to the conditioning signal.

items.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
items.summary: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges.

items.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
items.summary: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales.

items.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
items.summary: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage.

items.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
items.summary: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We provide theoretical analysis and conduct extensive experiments on a public indoor RME benchmark.

items.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training
items.summary: Conventional neural-network training typically follows a predefined optimization recipe, motivating a LLM agent that monitors training dynamics and adjusts optimizer settings as training progresses, but a fixed agent policy does not accumulate experience across runs.

items.title: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences
items.summary: Task instructions from users for agents are inherently underspecified, especially regarding safety boundaries--creating behavioral risks. To study these risks, we introduce BARC-Bench, a collection of 110 tasks across nine simulated workspace environments where benign requests leave openings for unsafe actions.

items.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
items.summary: Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information.

items.title: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help.

items.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
items.summary: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on.

items.title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon.

items.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
items.summary: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. We address this gap by introducing $M^3$, an automated red-teaming framework that formalizes multi-turn jailbreaking as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP).

items.title: Beyond On-Policy vs. Off-Policy: At What Level Should LLM Agent Distillation Follow the Student?
items.summary: Distilling interactive LLM agents requires choosing between teacher-generated demonstrations and student-generated experience, corresponding broadly to off-policy and on-policy distillation. Moreover, mixtures with identical teacher/student proportions at each level can yield substantially different performance, showing that how the two levels are paired matters beyond the overall amount of on-policy data.

items.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
items.summary: Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively.

items.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
items.summary: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. In this framework, a large-language-model (LLM) coding agent (Claude Opus 4.8) directly drives industry-standard electronic-design-automation (EDA) tools such as Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Calibre, Cadence EMX, and Ansys HFSS to design RF and mmWave modules.

items.title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
items.summary: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. We introduce Self-Direction, a mechanism for agents to learn from mistakes that combines the benefits of temporary in-context retries and policy updates. Ultimately, this self-directed repair transforms everyday mistakes into lasting lessons.

items.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
items.summary: We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. The author's toolkit grows as more papers are formalized, and authors can share their verified papers so that researchers who build on them can reuse their Lean code.

items.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
items.summary: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL.

items.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
items.summary: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. We introduce Phronix, a capability-centric learning paradigm that enables agentic harnesses to acquire, validate, and refine reusable capabilities from their own executions.
